title: Scaling the Next Paradigm of Heterogeneous Intelligence — Adrian Bertagnoli, Callosum
talk_summary: Adrian Bertagnoli argues that heterogeneous multi-agent systems (different models/architectures/hardware per subtask) beat single frontier models on cost and speed, citing recursive language models that treat context as a file environment and route sub-contexts to cheaper models. He shows benchmark results where offloading simple subtasks (e.g. zooming) to small models yields large cost/speed wins while matching frontier quality.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of stuffing a large context into the prompt, they put it in a file and let a coding agent query it programmatically (keyword search, regex, Python REPL), passing extracted sub-context to a recursive agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: treating the context as a um environment, rather than putting it all into the prompt
takeaways.numbers: 7x cheaper and 5x faster than GPT-5.2 on Oolong benchmark; 12x cheaper/3x faster with SambaNova

takeaways.what_they_do: Decompose a task into subtasks and route simple ones (e.g. zooming, visual reasoning) to small/cheap models, reserving frontier models for hard reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we offloaded that into less intelligent models because you don't need GPT to zoom for you
takeaways.numbers: 11x faster and 43x cheaper on those subtasks; overall 3.7x cheaper and 3x faster

takeaways.technique: Automated task-complexity classifier for model choice
takeaways.what_they_do: Started with hardcoded subtask→model mappings, then built an automation layer that predicts task complexity and picks the best-suited model/hardware.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have um created an automation layer that detects the task complexity and automatically predicts the best model

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat a task as a pipeline of heterogeneous sub-steps (visual, textual, etc.), each handled by a different model, rather than one model end-to-end.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the problem is heterogeneous uh it itself. It it decomposes into multiple steps
takeaways.numbers: Beat GPT-5.2 and Gemini 2.5 by 18% and 25% on VideoWebArena; 1.3x faster, 18x cheaper than GPT-5.2 alone

takeaways.what_they_do: Map workloads to different chips/hardware based on computational demand, including prefill/decode disaggregated systems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we choose different hardware depending on the computational demands on the agents
